overnightPermit.what: Olympic National Park wilderness permit, reserved in advance, per-night fee
overnightPermit.where: Reserve on Recreation.gov before the trip; there are no same-day walk-up permits. Bear canisters are required at Flapjack Lakes, and the Staircase trails are closed after the Bear Gulch Fire, so check status first.

overnightPermit.what: North Cascades National Park Service Complex backcountry permit, fee charged
overnightPermit.where: Reserve on Recreation.gov, or arrange it with the park the day before you travel; there is no permit office or cell service in Stehekin.

overnightPermit.what: Free self-issue wilderness permit (Henry M. Jackson or Alpine Lakes Wilderness)
overnightPermit.where: Fill one out at the trailhead kiosk.

add.name: Upper Swamp Creek basin
add.capacity: A few tent spots on heather and rock
add.water: Snowmelt and streams in the basin
add.permit: Same overnight permit as the rest of the trip
add.notes: Upper basin reached by the abandoned Swamp Creek trail and a Class 2-3 climb left of the waterfall. It puts the Dark Glacier in view and shortens the summit day. Brushy and slow to reach.

routes.note: Swamp Creek Camp is the standard base; the upper basin is the usual high camp but its elevation is approximate.

add.name: Bird Creek Camp
add.capacity: About three tents and a cook area
add.permit: Same overnight permit as the rest of the trip
add.notes: The only designated camp on the upper Devore Creek trail, just before the Bird Creek crossing. Parties base here and climb Flora in a long day, 4 to 5 hours up. Higher camps are possible in the larch basin around 6,500 to 6,900 ft.

routes.note: Real base is Bird Creek Camp on the Devore Creek trail, which was missing; its 4,200 ft elevation comes from one description only. The Company Creek entry describes a different approach.
